name: progress_is_render_owned
why: v2.9.0: PROGRESS.md has a single deterministic writer (the renderer, invoked by cursor advance); no with-lock choreography needed

name: has_track_mode_ref
why: v3.16.0 dispatch-shape rebuild: team-mode.md was renamed to track-mode.md.

name: no_quota_framing_for_pause
pattern: before quota runs out|pre-empts? quota exhaustion|quota[- ]driven pause

name: track_concurrency_is_nested_budget
pattern: one coordinator plus, at most, one active builder.{0,150}2 × tracks
why: v3.16.0: inverted/repurposed from team_mode_has_concurrency_cap, which pinned the old flat-agent-count 'concurrent teammate' phrasing. Under Option B concurrency is two-level (a nested budget, per plan risk #15) — this pins the actual nested-budget formula (2 × tracks) instead of a flat re-derived scalar.

name: pause_note_carries_team_state
why: v2.9.0: HANDOFF.md is retired; the paused cursor's body note carries resume context (team_name / queued tracks)

name: step0_merges_onto_working_branch
pattern: working branch now contains all recoverable work

name: wave_boundary_refactor_and_mutate
why: Mutation testing must survive as a wave-boundary step for EVERY dispatch shape. This assertion previously pinned 'Mutation testing after GREEN' in the old team-mode.md spawn prompt — the only PER-TASK mutation instruction in the plugin, and team-mode-exclusive. That prompt is gone (v3.16.0 track-mode rewrite), so track mode now has exact parity with task and solo mode: neither tdd-cycle (Red-Green-Refactor) nor shipyard-disciplined-builder has ever had a per-task mutate step. Repointed rather than deleted so the surviving system-wide guarantee stays guarded. NOTE a pre-existing overclaim this exposed, not caused by the rewrite: ship-execute/SKILL.md:12 says 'Every task follows Red -> Green -> Refactor -> Mutate', but Mutate has only ever run at the wave boundary (wave_N_refactor), never inside a task.

name: workaround_inline_rules_scope_discipline
why: v3.16.0: repointed from the old team-mode.md 'Inline Rules' section (retired — track mode has no custom-authored spawn prompt anymore) to the shared, unchanged shipyard-disciplined-builder agent's own scope-discipline rule (item 3), which every dispatch shape — solo, task, and track's nested builders — already goes through.

name: no_team_manual_worktree_workaround
pattern: Create worktrees manually|git worktree add -b shipyard/wt
why: Phase 3 mode-semantics correction: #37549 is a platform design decision (teams isolate by file-partition, not directory) — there is no manual-worktree workaround to preserve; teammates share the main working tree.

name: no_37549_workaround_claim
why: v3.16.0: inverted from workaround_team_bug_37549. Under the corrected design #37549 isn't a bug — track mode always passes isolation: "worktree" explicitly, so nothing about #37549 applies and there is nothing to work around (git-strategy.md states this explicitly: '#37549 is not in this table — it isn't a bug and there is no workaround to document'). A naive repoint of the old contains-check would pass for the wrong reason (track-mode.md does mention #37549 once, but to say it does NOT apply) — inverted to a regression guard instead.

name: no_team_cd_worktree_path
why: Phase 3: teammates operate directly in the shared working tree; there is no per-teammate WORKTREE_PATH to cd into.

name: no_team_shared_working_tree_claim
why: v3.16.0: inverted from team_shares_one_working_tree. Track mode is the OPPOSITE of the old model it pinned — every task (including every nested builder) gets its own worktree and branch, and the coordinator itself is worktree-isolated too. Inverted to a regression guard against the old, now-false 'one shared working tree' framing ever coming back.

name: no_per_task_wt_branches_claim
pattern: NO per-task .?wt-\*.? branches|no per-feature worktree or branch
why: v3.16.0: inverted from team_no_per_task_wt_branches. Track mode now DOES have per-task wt-* branches (one per nested builder, per §4.2's one-task-one-worktree-one-branch invariant) — the opposite of the old team-mode claim. Positive coverage of the new invariant is added separately (nested_builders_get_worktree_isolation); this is retained as a regression guard against the old, now-false claim reappearing.

name: workaround_precheck_covers_both_modes
why: v3.16.0: vocabulary update — the heading is now 'Pre-spawn Branch Check (task AND track mode)', matching the solo/task/track rename; the check itself (verify orchestrator branch before spawning worktree agents) is unchanged.

name: workaround_bug_docs_worktree_table
why: v3.16.0: #37549 was deliberately REMOVED from this table (it isn't a bug — see bug_37549_reclassified_not_workaround below), so the pattern no longer requires it. #34645/#34775 remain, unaffected.

name: bug_37549_reclassified_not_workaround
pattern: 37549 is not in this table|isn't a bug and there is no workaround
why: v3.16.0: positive coverage of the corrected #37549 framing (a platform design decision, not a bug — track mode always passes isolation: "worktree" explicitly, so nothing applies) that git-strategy.md now states explicitly in place of the removed table row.

name: workaround_bug_docs_already_on_worktree
pattern: Already on a worktree branch.*pre-spawn branch check

name: wave_boundary_uses_scoped_tests
pattern: WAVE-SCOPED tests|wave-scoped tests|scoped tests for wave

name: wave_boundary_no_full_integration
pattern: Delegate INTEGRATION tests to a test subagent

name: full_suite_only_at_sprint_completion
pattern: Full test suite|full test suite.*sprint completion|only time the entire suite runs

name: prohibits_bash_redirect_for_state
pattern: Never use .?`?echo`?.*(redirect|shell|state)|Never use `echo`, `printf`, or shell redirects

name: resume_uses_event_log_as_source_of_truth
pattern: event log is the source of truth|event log.*authoritative

name: auto_loop_sentinel_written_before_skill_call
pattern: sets .auto_loop_attempted: true. on the cursor itself|MUST land before the .Skill
why: v3.1: cursor bootstrap-check sets the auto_loop_attempted sentinel as a side effect BEFORE the model invokes Skill(loop), so the /loop iteration-1 re-entry sees it and skips re-bootstrapping.

name: auto_loop_cleanup_on_terminal
pattern: does not carry .?auto_loop_attempted.? forward|do NOT carry .?auto_loop_attempted

name: wakeup_leak_protection_three_conditions_named
pattern: cursor .?terminal: true.?, SPRINT\.md .?status: completed.?, or no active sprint|all THREE conditions
why: the three dead-sprint conditions must stay named in the sweep instruction

name: wakeup_leak_protection_emits_pipeline_terminal_on_noop
why: v2.9.0: the noop emit is done by `shipyard-data cursor noop` (emit-first is pinned in test_cursor_cli.mjs); the skill must route through it with the canonical reason

name: wakeup_leak_protection_prints_cycle_complete_marker
pattern: CYCLE COMPLETE — sprint already complete\. /loop should stop\.

name: bootstrap_runs_after_noop_terminal_sweep
pattern: Auto-loop bootstrap \(run AFTER the no-op terminal sweep

name: bootstrap_refuses_dead_sprint
pattern: never reports eligible for a dead/absent/completed sprint|Never bootstrap .?/loop.? against a dead sprint
why: v3.1: eligibility is CLI-owned (cursor bootstrap-check); it never reports eligible for a dead/absent/completed sprint (the v2.2.0 wakeup-leak precondition).

name: bootstrap_dead_sprint_emits_terminal
pattern: sprint-liveness re-check|never reports eligible for a dead
why: v3.1: the dead-sprint guard moved into cursor bootstrap-check's sprint-liveness re-check; the model no longer emits a sprint_dead_at_bootstrap noop (the step-3 no-op sweep already handles dead sprints).

name: v250_background_dispatch_documented
pattern: Background dispatch \(the default for wave-dispatch in v2\.5\.0\+\)

name: v250_pending_subagents_cursor_field
why: v2.9.0: pending_subagents is passed to cursor advance as a JSON k=v; the CLI renders the YAML list

name: v250_background_capture_file_path_canonical
why: v3.1: builders persist via `shipyard-data task-return` to `.subagent-returns/<task_id>.json` (was a freeform .txt).

name: v250_orchestrator_never_reads_agent_return_in_bg
pattern: orchestrator never reads the Agent tool's return value in background mode

name: v250_recovery_runs_identical_gate_logic
pattern: IDENTICAL logic that runs in sync mode|same orchestrator-side gate

name: v250_redispatch_is_sync_not_background
pattern: redispatch is itself a sync dispatch|Redispatch is always SYNC

name: handoff_next_up_framed_as_separate_cycle
pattern: SEPARATE cycle you start yourself|separate cycle the user starts|does NOT (chain into|continue into) /ship-review

name: handoff_stop_marker_is_final_signal
pattern: reads the LAST line as its continue-or-stop signal|MUST be the final line

name: loop_leak_detection_is_cli_owned
why: v2.9.0: repeat-leak detection runs inside `cursor noop` (pinned in test_cursor_cli.mjs); the skill documents it

name: preflight_advances_to_salvage
why: Fresh start creates the cursor at preflight; the preflight handler must close with an advance to salvage (the next documented advance was ->load, illegal from preflight).

name: auto_loop_uses_bootstrap_check_cli
why: v3.1: the entire auto-loop eligibility computation is CLI-owned via `cursor bootstrap-check`; the model no longer computes the 5 predicates.

name: cursor_resume_documented
why: Escalated/paused cursors are recovered via `cursor resume execute` (flips back to in_progress at the recorded stage).

name: escalated_terminal_recovery_at_entry
pattern: status: escalated.*resumable|escalated.*NOT a completed sprint|escalated \(recoverable\) halt
why: The entry recipe must distinguish an escalated terminal (recoverable, resumable) from a completed one (leaked wakeup).

name: parked_task_terminal_handoff
pattern: parked.*(hand.*/ship-review|does not block sprint completion)|hand them to /ship-review
why: A parked task (task_blocked evidence) satisfies its terminal-gate slot; a needs-attention sprint CAN terminate and hands parked tasks to /ship-review.

name: recovery_handler_anchors_and_emits
why: Background recovery must anchor each gate-passed commit AND emit task_dispatch_returned status=complete (the single orchestrator choke point) — background mode was missing both, reopening the v2.8 orphan vector.

name: waiting_timeout_taskstop_zombie
why: On genuine timeout the background Agent handle must be TaskStop'd so a zombie builder can't keep committing.

name: waiting_liveness_check_before_timeout
why: Before declaring a subagent TIMED OUT, check for a recent task_loop_iteration event — a live slow builder is not dead.

name: parked_branch_salvage_not_merged
why: A parked task's worktree branch is anchored + force-removed (not merged) so verify-wave-integrated Check A passes without merging unverified work.

name: expensive_stage_pauses_before_askuser
why: sprint_full_build failure and demo-probe failure/absence pause the cursor BEFORE AskUserQuestion so a /loop wakeup can't re-run the whole stage and re-ask.

name: unconfigured_build_still_advances
pattern: unconfigured, still advance as a pass-through tick|unconfigured, advance as a pass-through
why: The stage graph has no skip edges; unconfigured build/full-build stages still advance as pass-through ticks.

name: task_hotfix_guard_refuses_active_sprint
pattern: Finish or pause it.*before running --task/--hotfix|A sprint is active.*--task
why: --task/--hotfix must refuse when a non-terminal sprint cursor exists (they'd clobber the sprint cursor).

name: task_hotfix_guard_refuses_terminal_current
why: v3.4.0: --task/--hotfix also refuse a TERMINAL execute cursor still in current/ (execute done, review pending) — never --force.

name: readiness_banner_no_ask
pattern: invoking `/ship-execute` IS the consent to execute|advance straight to `wave_1_dispatch`
why: v3.4.0: fresh-start readiness states a banner and advances; the Begin/Adjust/Abort ask is removed.

name: readiness_anomaly_prompt_conditional
pattern: the ONLY ask on a fresh start|one ask max, zero when clean
why: v3.4.0: the single readiness ask fires only on baseline-fail / branch-mismatch / wt-* branch / dirty tree.

name: paused_wakeup_inert
why: v3.4.0: a /loop wakeup on a paused cursor runs cursor noop and STOPS; resume is a user-only decision.

name: paused_noop_awaiting_user_reason
why: v3.4.0: the paused/escalated wakeup noop emits reason=awaiting_user_<paused|escalated>.

name: tick_never_exits_with_pending_question
pattern: tick NEVER exits with a pending question and no marker
why: v3.4.0: the tick-exit contract states the pause-before-blocking-ask rule once.

name: park_uses_task_set_status_blocked
why: v3.6.0 wave 2: Park handling routes through the task-state CLI, which writes blocked_reason/blocked_since atomically and auto-emits task_blocked.

name: park_does_not_double_emit_task_blocked
pattern: Emit `shipyard-data events emit task_blocked task=<id> reason="<short>" escalation=<code>`
why: v3.6.0 wave 2: the old Park-handling sentence emitted task_blocked manually; task set-status blocked now auto-emits it, so a separate emit would double the event. Scoped to the OLD PARK SENTENCE specifically (not a blanket ban on the phrase). Follow-up (needs-attention now CLI-covered): dispatching-task-loop's persistent-failure/presumed_dead paths were migrated to `task set-status ... needs-attention --reason ...`, which deliberately does NOT auto-emit task_blocked (documented as distinct from blocked) — see spec-state-cli's TASK_HELD_STATUS_FIELDS comment.

name: salvage_uses_task_set_status_needs_attention
why: v3.6.0 wave 2 follow-up: needs-attention transitions (salvage persistent-failure, timeout) route through the task-state CLI now that it covers this status.

name: uses_lock_acquire_execution
why: v3.7.0 wave 3: Acquire Locks section routes through shipyard-data lock acquire execution instead of the acquiring-skill-lock prose procedure.

name: uses_lock_release
why: v3.7.0 wave 3: abnormal-exit manual release routes through shipyard-data lock release execution.

name: no_hand_write_lock_file
why: v3.7.0 wave 3: skill-mutex lock files are CLI-owned — no skill body hand-Writes them anymore.

name: zero_thinking_doctrine
why: v3.10.0: the shell's Operating Principles state the zero-thinking doctrine as the first bullet — the shell executes the checklist and escalates judgment calls, it does not reason about them.

name: no_experimental_env_gate_claim
why: v3.16.0: inverted from team_is_experimental_opt_in. D6 (plan §3.2) fixed the shipped defect of gating track/team dispatch on this env var, which no longer selects a distinct platform capability (F1: team_name is deprecated and ignored; isolation is the only real discriminator). Inverted to a regression guard against the env-gate coming back, rather than a repoint (the phrase is correctly absent everywhere now, including track-mode.md).

name: verification_spine_delegation_independent
why: v3.16.0: repointed to track-mode.md; the exact v3.10.0 phrase 'delegation-shape-independent' isn't restated verbatim, but the same invariant is — 'A coordinator cannot self-certify ... and a nested builder cannot self-certify ... A track cannot self-certify either way.' Pattern updated to match the actual (stronger, since C1 makes it structural rather than a stated rule) text while preserving the semantic guarantee this assertion pins.

name: team_task_return_mandatory
pattern: Persist the structured return via the CLI \(MANDATORY\)
why: v3.16.0: repointed from team-mode.md's own (now-retired) custom spawn prompt to the shared, unchanged shipyard-disciplined-builder agent that track mode nests unchanged for every task — the MANDATORY-persist-return-first guarantee is now provided once, centrally, for every dispatch shape (solo/task/track) instead of being duplicated in a team-mode-specific prompt. Same text already independently pinned by dispatching-task-loop.json's v250_subagent_writes_capture_file; kept here too since ship-execute.json is specifically about the whole shell's correctness including its track dispatch path.

name: team_no_taskreturn_is_blocked
why: v3.16.0: repointed to the shared shipyard-disciplined-builder agent (Required Return Shape: 'Done-without-task-return is a contract violation'), which every nested track builder now runs unchanged. Stronger than the v3.10.0 original: under C1 a nested builder has no TaskUpdate at all in its isolated context, so self-certification is structurally impossible, not merely against the rules.

name: team_wave_boundary_integration_gate
why: v3.16.0: repointed to track-mode.md; pattern updated to match the actual Wave Boundary Protocol wording ('...THEN `shipyard-data verify-wave-integrated`, THEN teardown') rather than the old team-mode.md phrasing. Same invariant (integration gate runs before any teardown) is preserved.

name: render_provenance_negation
why: v3.11.0 context-conflation fix: the render-before-ask rule must state the negative — Read results, subagent returns, dossier files, and SendMessage payloads are not 'shown to the user'. Anchors the same phrase check_render_before_ask requires.

name: track_coordinator_never_commits_or_writes
why: v3.16.0 WP5 addition: §4.2 property 1/2 — a coordinator has no Write/Edit/Bash tool, so it cannot commit or leave uncommitted work; pins the agent's own stated rule.

name: track_coordinator_tools_allowlist_exact
why: v3.16.0 WP5 addition: pins the exact frontmatter tools allowlist — no Bash/Write/Edit is what makes 'never commits, never writes, cannot forge a task-return' structural rather than a stated rule (§4.2 property 2).

name: track_coordinator_wave_scoped
why: v3.16.0 WP5 addition: §4.2 property 1 — a coordinator surviving a wave boundary would fork builders from a stale wave-N base and silently drop wave-N's merged work, the same class of data loss as the v2.8.x baseRef incident. Coordinators must be spawned fresh per wave.

name: nested_builders_get_worktree_isolation
why: v3.16.0 WP5 addition: every nested builder a track coordinator dispatches gets isolation: "worktree", same as task-mode builders — one task = one worktree = one branch = one commit, so the incident-hardened verification spine applies unchanged.

name: sendmessage_correct_shape
why: v3.16.0 WP5 addition: D2 fix — the real SendMessage schema is {to, message, summary}, additionalProperties:false. The old team-mode.md used the wrong {type, recipient, content} shape everywhere, which would fail validation on every call.

name: sendmessage_no_stale_recipient_field
why: v3.16.0 WP5 addition: regression guard against D2's wrong field name ({recipient: ...} instead of {to: ...}) reappearing.

name: isolated_agents_no_task_star_c1
why: v3.16.0 WP5 addition: pins C1 (§2.1/§3.1 of the plan) — isolated agents (track coordinators and nested builders alike) have no TaskCreate/TaskUpdate/TaskList, so main is the sole owner of the Task* checklist in every dispatch shape.

name: governance_mode_never_silently_overridden
pattern: declared or forced mode is honored, never silently overridden
why: v3.16.0 WP5 addition: §4.5 governance rule — a declared execution_mode is honored or surfaced via AskUserQuestion, never silently decided by the shell. This is the P1 defect (a zero-thinking shell silently overrode an explicit user-set mode) that motivated the whole rebuild.

name: governance_mode_deviation_not_escalation_routed
why: v3.16.0 WP5 addition: §4.5 — mode-deviation concerns go to AskUserQuestion (a user-authority decision), never to escalating-to-thinker (reasoning-gap consults only, and mode selection isn't one of its seven triggers).

name: wave_task_checklist_created
why: Phase 6: a high-level, mirror-only per-wave task checklist is created once wave structure is known from SPRINT.md

name: wave_task_subject_prefix_distinct
why: Phase 6: the [sprint-<id>] prefix keeps the wave mirror distinguishable from ship-sprint's [sprint-plan] Step N: checklist. (v3.16.0: updated — under the dispatch-shape rebuild there is no longer a separate per-teammate checklist to distinguish this from; main is the sole Task* owner in every dispatch shape, per C1.)

name: wave_task_gated_completion
why: Phase 6: a wave task is marked completed only after verify-wave-integrated passes and the cursor advances, never on a builder's return claim alone

name: wave_task_list_never_authority
pattern: wave task list is a progress surface and a recovery anchor, NEVER authority
why: Phase 6: mirrors the ship-sprint/ship-discuss guardrail so no behavior ever gates on TaskList state for the pipeline

name: wave_task_recovery_anchor
why: Phase 6: compaction recovery / re-entry calls TaskList() first as a position anchor, confirmed against the cursor + event log
